# Chapter
Introduction

This document provides information on STM32G031x4/x6/x8 microcontrollers, such as description, functional overview, pin assignment and definition, electrical characteristics, packaging, and ordering codes.

Information on memory mapping and control registers is object of reference manual.

Information on Arm code Cortex-M0+ core is available from the www.arm.com website.

a. Arm is a registered trademark of Arm Limited (or its subsidiaries) in the US and/or elsewhere.

Description

The STM32G031x4/x6/x8 mainstream microcontrollers are based on high-performance Arm® Cortex®-M0+ 32-bit RISC core operating at up to 64 MHz frequency. Offering a high level of integration, they are suitable for a wide range of applications in consumer, industrial and appliance domains and ready for the Internet of Things (IoT) solutions.
The devices incorporate a memory protection unit (MPU), high-speed embedded memories (up to 64 Kbytes of Flash program memory and 8 Kbytes of SRAM), DMA and an extensive range of system functions, enhanced I/Os and peripherals. The devices offer standard communication interfaces (two I²Cs, two SPIs / one I²S, and two USARTs), one 12-bit ADC (2.5 MSps) with up to 19 channels, an internal voltage reference buffer, a low-power RTC, an advanced control PWM timer running at up to double the CPU frequency, four general-purpose 16-bit timers, a 32-bit general-purpose timer, two low-power 16-bit timers, two watchdog timers, and a SysTick timer.
The devices operate within ambient temperatures from -40 to 125°C. They can operate with supply voltages from 1.7 V to 3.6 V. Optimized dynamic consumption combined with a comprehensive set of power-saving modes, low-power timers and low-power UART, allows the design of low-power applications.
VBAT direct battery input allows keeping RTC and backup registers powered.
The devices come in packages with 8 to 48 pins.

### 5.3.12 Electrical sensitivity characteristics

Based on three different tests (ESD, LU) using specific measurement methods, the device is stressed in order to determine its performance in terms of electrical sensitivity.

**Electrostatic discharge (ESD)**

Electrostatic discharges (a positive then a negative pulse separated by 1 second) are applied to the pins of each sample according to each pin combination. The sample size depends on the number of supply pins in the device (3 parts × (n+1) supply pins). This test conforms to the ANSI/JEDEC standard.

**Table 48. ESD absolute maximum ratings**

| Symbol | Ratings                                          | Conditions               | Class | Maximum value<sup>(1)</sup> | Unit |
|--------|----------------------------------------------------|----------------------------|-------|--------------------------|------|
|        | Electrostatic discharge voltage (human body model)| 𝑇<sub>A</sub> = +25 °C, conforming to ANSI/ESDA/JEDEC JS-001 | 1C      | 1000                    | V    |
|        | Electrostatic discharge voltage (charge device model)| 𝑇<sub>A</sub> = +25 °C, conforming to ANSI/ESDA/JEDEC JS-002 | C2a    | 500                     |      |
1. Based on characterization results, not tested in production.

**Static latch-up**

Two complementary static tests are required on six parts to assess the latch-up performance:
- A supply overvoltage is applied to each power supply pin.
- A current is injected to each input, output and configurable I/O pin.

These tests are compliant with EIA/JESD 78A IC latch-up standard.

**Table 49. Electrical sensitivity**

**(a) Interfacing Method (Figure 42)**
- **Device Connection**:
  - The front-end CCD (Charge-Coupled Device) chip is connected to photo-electron multipliers.
  - The photo-electronic multipliers are connected to the encoder drivers located on the cavity supporting PCB (Printed Circuit Board).
  - The output signals from the photo-electronic industry are processed electrostatically and digitized.

**(b) Interfacing Methods (Tables 9 and 10)**
- The schematic diagrams provided were downloaded from the online environment and visualized using Adobe Photoshop.

**(c) Circuit Analysis Performance Curve (Figure 43)**
- The performance curve of the decoder top grisp circuit with P-D2-01 as the decoding CPU is listed with respect to values of compute sequences. The performance curve is plotted on the graph paper, showing a clear trend of increasing performance as the sequence continues.

**(d) Picture of the Stage with P-D2-01 as the ASC (Advanced Signal Conditioning) CPU (Figure 44)**
- The picture shows the stage with P-D2-01 as the ASC CPU.
  - The stage contains the rectangular object particle detector with a diameter of 53 mm surrounded by three other star-shaped objects.
  - Two electronics boxes are fitted adjacent to the stage.
  - The stage is connected to the optical table for positioning.
  - The stage and electronic boxes are imported from the science laboratory through metal-framed racks.
  - The electronic boxes are self-built and consist of a main board and a protection cover.
  - The main board  has FPGA based multiplex configuration assisted by RTL 7650, which has 32 FPGA channels.
  - The protection cover is a fold with cut-out sections as depending wisely on optimizing the emission data throughput, different outputs could be output.
  - The protective covers on plastic boards are easily removed so that maintenance personnel without configuration can modify the setups.

**(e) Picture of the Stage and Electronics Box with ASIC CPUs installed (Figure 45)**
- The picture shows the stage with P-D2-01 as the ASC CPU.
  - The stage contains the object particle detector with a diameter of 53 mm.
  - Two electronics boxes are fitted adjacent to the stage.
  - The stage and boxes are imported from the science laboratory.
  - The electronic boxes are self-built with a Dummy adapter box.

**(f) Plastic Bird(Sections 10 and 11)**
- **Sample Configuration**:
  - The cases for the cryostat are made from fluoride plastic (CTE: 1.1 x 10^-6 K^-1).
  - The plastic material from packaging will be recycled and re-processed as a separate component, with无锡院所A6807 as the cause.

**6.9.2 Selecting the product temperature range**

# As applications do not commonly use microcontrollers at their maximum power consumption, it is useful to calculate the exact power consumption and junction temperature todetermine which temperature range best suits the application.

# The following example shows how to calculate the temperature range needed for a givenapplication.

# Example:

# Assuming the following worst application conditions:

- ambient temperature \(T_A = 50 °C\) (measured according to JESD51-2)

- \(I_{DD} = 50 mA; V_{DD} = 3.6 V\)

- 20 I/Os simultaneously used as output at low level with \(I_{OL} = 8 mA\) (\(V_{OL} = 0.4 V\)), and

- 8 I/Os simultaneously used as output at low level with \(I_{OL} = 20 mA\) (\(V_{OL} = 1.3 V\)),

# the power consumption from power supply \(P_{INT}\) is:


\[
P_{INT} = 50 mA \times 3.6 V = 118 mW,
\]

# the power loss through I/Os \(P_{IO}\) is


\[
P_{IO} = 20 \times 8 mA \times 0.4 V + 8 \times 20 mA \times 1.3 V = 272 mW,
\]

# and the total power \(P_D\) to dissipate is:

\[
P_D = 180 mW + 272 mW = 452 mW
\]

# For product in LQFP48 with \(\Theta_{JA} = 75 °C/W\), the junction temperature stabilizes at:


\[
T_J = 50 °C + (75 °C/W \times 452 mW) = 50 °C + 33.9 °C = 83.9 °C
\]

# As a conclusion, product version with suffix 6 (maximum allowed \(T_J = 105 °C\)) is sufficient for this application.

# If the same application was used in a hot environment with maximum \(T_A\) greater than \(71 °C\), the junction temperature would exceed \(105 °C\) and the product version with suffix 3 (maximum allowed \(T_J = 125 °C\)) would have to be ordered.
